Research life / Personal reflections

Moving to France for Postdoc position

By Rohit Shrivastava · 3 min read

Bonjour et bienvenue

During PhD, I decided to broaden my area of expertise and work in new area of research for my postdoctoral training. At that time I was keen to work on host immune response to parasitic infection. This was obvious choice as I had experience of working on Leishmania parasites so logic extension of my skills to apply them to host immune response. However, it didn’t materialise as I had no skills or experience of working in immunology. But in all the postdoctoral applications I sent I was trying hard to go out of my comfort zone.

During the time of applying, I submitted an application to work on small ubiquitin-like modifier, NEDD8. To apply I read 2 review articles and 2 papers from the lab to which I was applying. I wrote a cover letter mentioning that I wish to investigate the role of Protein Quality Control machinery during neurodegeneration. To my utter surprise I got an email for skype interview. It was long yet comfortable interview. During interview, I got to know that final decision for the selection will be made by a committee based on the PIs comments. Next day I also send additional suggestions to my future PI about the research project that I wish to pursue. About 2 months later I got another email saying I have been selected for 2nd round of interview. We again had a skype interview and this time it was more technical and scientific discussion on a previous paper from the lab. One month later I got to know I have been selected for the position. I was delighted to finally have something to look forward to after PhD. However, it crashed my plans to rest for 2-3 months before starting the new position. But it is rightly said whatever happens, happens for good.

For my visa formalities I was in contact with the academic secretary who was super nice and patiently answered my queries. However, I got delayed in submitting my thesis. In order to obtain a “Convention d’Accueil” or the hosting agreement University need thesis acceptance letter but I had thesis submission letter. I tried to explain that in Israeli universities there is no thesis defence like in European universities and a thesis acceptance letter will be issued once thesis has been accepted by all the evaluators. After a fair bit of explaining, finally everything was ok and I got the hosting letter and applied for visa. There was no special formalities for French Passport Talent Visa and got my visa in 10 days. In fact Consulate staff at Tel Aviv was super nice and prompt in replying to emails. Without knowing a word of french or confirmed place to stay or any clue of the spread of coronavirus I took a night flight to reach Montpellier the next morning.
